title: James Carville says Russia has 'got something on' Trump
text:
Democratic strategist James Carville said he believes Russia has compromising material on President Donald Trump, arguing that the president’s approach toward Russian President Vladimir Putin leaves him with no other explanation.

Carville made the claim on September 10 on the "Politics War Room" podcast after co-host Al Hunt shared a listener’s theory that Trump “is working for Putin.”

“I think he’s getting his marching orders from Russia, maybe China,” Hunt read from the listener’s comment. “He’s actively undermining our country. Am I crazy?”

Carville responded, “No, mademoiselle, you’re not crazy.”

Carville pointed to Trump’s handling of Russia and recent interactions involving Steve Witkoff, the U.S. special envoy to the Middle East and special envoy for Peace Missions, and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, another of the president's peace envoys.

“And the evidence is this,” Carville said. “Representing the United States of America in a critical issue of war and peace. Steve Witkoff — oh, come on, man! — goes to Russia and says, ‘Putin is one of’ — who is, by the way, by any definition, an international criminal of the first order! Maybe an international criminal is better than anybody else — he talks about what a great person he is and all the things that he’s done and how honored he is.”

Carville also criticized Kushner’s involvement, saying he could not understand the administration’s posture toward Moscow without believing Trump was compromised.

“Oh, come on! And he was, of course, he was there with Jared Kushner, who also has nothing to do with the United States government. Our friend in France, you make an observation — I don’t know any other explanation! I know of no other explanation!” he said.

Carville revived an unsubstantiated allegation about purported compromising footage involving Trump during a 2013 visit to Moscow.

“And everything that Trump does, he does exactly what Putin would want him to do. I’m sorry, I have always thought, and I continue to believe, there is a p** tape,” he declared.

Carville acknowledged he did not know what the alleged compromising material might contain but remained convinced Russia possessed something damaging.

“Now whether or not it’s him p***** on a pros****** in Moscow, I don’t know — but what I mean is, compromise,” he explained, as reported by Mediaite. “They’ve got something on this guy. They just have to have it, ’cause nothing else makes sense.”
